hiring_bar_summary.summary: High, centralized bar: practical coding depth plus system design and a behavioral round that also probes past technical work. This is a qualitative synthesis, not a measured pass rate — Datadog publishes no applicant-to-offer rate in the fetched sources.

evidence.claim: Engineer-reported loop: recruiter call, technical phone screen, then an onsite with coding, system design and behavioral rounds; staff roles substitute a project presentation for one coding round.

screening_signals.claim: Official candidate page: one interview step is expected to happen in person.
Official candidate page: AI tools are restricted during interviews; misuse or non-disclosure can lead to disqualification.
Engineer-reported: system-design performance is used for leveling, and shallow design answers can result in a down-level.

process_stages.claim: Official high-level structure: initial conversation, face-to-face interviews (possibly multiple rounds or panels), a possible take-home project depending on role, and for some roles an executive interview, then selection.
Engineer-reported SWE sequence: recruiter call (about 30 min), technical phone screen (about 1 hour), onsite (about 4 hours).

interview_styles.claim: Practical, layered coding problems (starting from a familiar algorithmic core, then adding product-like complexity), system design, and behavioral questions that include technical detail on past work.

thesis_text: Bottom line: Datadog is a realistic but demanding SWE target best approached through a specific open role, with preparation weighted to practical coding and system design rather than puzzle volume. Who gets in (sourced numbers only): no population numbers are claimed in this record — no public sample of Datadog hires was sourceable in this pass, so school, feeder and major shares are intentionally omitted. The only process numbers here come from engineer-reported coverage (recruiter call about 30 minutes, phone screen about 1 hour, onsite about 4 hours, total about 6 weeks), labeled anecdotal. Stated vs revealed screens: Datadog states a role-dependent structure — initial conversation, face-to-face rounds, a possible take-home, and an executive interview for some roles, with one step in person and strict interview AI rules. Engineer reports reveal a centralized loop where team matching happens only after the onsite and where system-design depth drives leveling. Ranked entry routes: (1) direct application to a specific SWE posting, (2) intern/new-grad pipeline kept as a separate cohort, (3) referral or recruiter outreach as an entry accelerant with unquantified weight. Timeline/dates (as of 2026-10-12): no official SWE application window was published on the fetched pages; engineer-reported end-to-end time is about 6 weeks — re-verify before relying on it. Risks/alternatives: the centralized, committee-style bar means a strong candidate can pass and still wait on team matching; adjacent observability/infrastructure employers are the natural hedge. Gap analysis against a specific user profile is not computed in this record (no population sample).
known_biases_of_data: Survivorship bias: public interview guides reflect people who reached or completed loops, not rejected applicants.
Self-report bias: interviewing.io content is based on conversations with engineers and cross-checked anecdotes, not Datadog HR data.
Official careers pages are employer marketing and describe the intended process, which may differ by team, level and region.
No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass; sponsorship and school patterns are therefore unstated, not negative findings.
